docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Specification-Driven Frameworks

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04 and M3-04, or equivalent Copilot and custom-agent experience

Duration: 4 hours (1 hour trainer content, 3 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Use Hypervelocity Engineering (HVE), a structured engineering framework for GitHub Copilot, to take a feature from research to reviewed code. You start with its file-based Research, Plan, Implement, Review (RPI) workflow. Each phase writes a file the next phase reads.

If time allows, you also add repository instructions, a coding standard, and a custom review agent, and use Product Manager Advisor and Agile Coach to refine the feature before implementation.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Explain RPI, HVE's agents, prompts, and instructions, and why phases hand off through files.
  • Run direct HVE Research, Plan, Implement, and Review phases and read each .copilot-tracking/ file.
  • Compare direct phase prompts with the combined /rpi and its Follow-up step.
  • Deliver and review one containerized API slice.
  • Optional: add project context, an applyTo coding instruction, and a custom agent, and check that each is active.
  • Optional: use Product Manager Advisor and Agile Coach to refine the story and criteria.

docs.title: HVE Core requirement
docs.text: The hands-on challenge requires HVE Core (the extension or Copilot CLI plugin). Without it, learners can read trainer-provided files but can't do the lab. Keep .copilot-tracking/ local and ignored by Git.

docs.title: HVE references
docs.text:
HVE commands and generated files change between versions. Check the HVE Core README for your version before you teach.

  • HVE Core repository and framework overview
  • Install HVE Core
  • RPI workflow overview
  • Using RPI together
  • Why RPI works

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/ Slides slides.md Lab lab/ Starter brief and project lab/starter/ Trainer reference solution lab/solution/ HVE artifact reference lab/solution/hve-artifacts.md

docs.title: HVE Core challenge
docs.text: From product intent to reviewed code

docs.title: What HVE is
docs.text:
Hypervelocity Engineering is a structured engineering framework for GitHub Copilot.

It gives agent work defined roles, standards, human review gates, and saved phase files.

Command names change between versions. Check the HVE Core README for your version.

docs.title: RPI in one slide
docs.text:
Research → Plan → Implement → Review, then Follow-up.

Phase Prompt Writes Research /rpi-research What exists, limits, rejected options Plan /rpi-plan Tasks, acceptance criteria, checks, critique Implement /rpi-implement Code and a changes log Review /rpi-review Per-criterion verdicts and a decision

Follow-up sends defects to Implement, decision gaps to Plan, and evidence gaps to Research.

docs.title: Four component types
docs.text: Component Job Agents Own roles and multi-step protocols Prompts Start repeatable workflows Instructions Apply standards by file pattern Tracking artifacts Carry state between phases

docs.title: File as interface
docs.text:
Each phase writes a Markdown file. The next phase reads that file, not the chat.

.copilot-tracking/research/<date>/<task>-research.md
  → plans/<date>/<task>-plan.md  (+ critique under reviews/plans/)
  → changes/<date>/<task>-changes.md
  → reviews/logs/<date>/<task>-review.md

You can read, diff, and edit a file, then attach it to a fresh chat and carry on. Paths vary by version.

docs.title: Research before code
docs.text:
Research answers:

  • Which files own the behavior?
  • What constraints already exist?
  • Which alternatives were rejected?
  • What check could disprove the approach?

Output: .copilot-tracking/research/

docs.title: Plan before implementation
docs.text:
Plan maps criteria to files, checks, dependencies, and human gates.

Output:

.copilot-tracking/plans/

docs.title: Implement and Review
docs.text:
Implement follows the approved plan and writes a changes log.

Review checks whether the result meets the request, code quality standards, tests, and instructions.

The human still decides: approve, request changes, or pause.

docs.title: Direct and combined RPI
docs.text:
Direct prompts Combined /rpi task="..." You type One prompt per phase One prompt for the task Approval You approve each phase Depends on the mode you pick Output One file per phase The same kinds of files, one task name After Review You route defects Follow-up routes them Use it when Learning, demos, approvals The team trusts the handoffs

Both write the same files. Combined only changes who drives.

docs.title: Optional: HVE customization is additive
docs.text:
.github/copilot-instructions.md
.github/instructions/*.instructions.md
.github/agents/*.agent.md

Project context reaches all agents. Custom agents add repository-owned roles and output contracts.

An instruction loads by applyTo glob, set in its frontmatter:

applyTo: "src/**/*.js,tests/**/*.test.js"

Copilot loads it only when working on a matching file.

docs.title: Check that it's active
docs.text:
Creating a file doesn't mean HVE used it.

File Check Instructions Edit a matching file, ask a question. The file shows in References. A non-matching file doesn't load it Agent It appears in the agent picker (/agent in the CLI). Its answer follows your format Prompt Typing /name shows it in the picker, and it runs

Then find one plan, code, or review change it caused.

docs.title: Optional: HVE starts before engineering
docs.text:
Business idea
  → BRD Builder / Product Manager Advisor / PRD Builder
  → Agile Coach
  → RPI
  → reviewed code

BRD: business requirements, why the business wants this. PRD: product requirements, what the product must do. @BRD Builder and @PRD Builder write them.

Product Manager Advisor tests value and assumptions. Agile Coach turns intent into a user story and acceptance criteria. The lab starts from a supplied product intent.

docs.title: Challenge sequence
docs.text:
1. Run direct Research and Plan prompts.
  2. Run Implement and Review.
  3. Compare the result with combined /rpi.

Optional, if time allows, before Implement: add repository context, an applyTo instruction, and a custom reviewer, and use Product Manager Advisor and Agile Coach.

docs.title: Build the endpoint
docs.text: Deliver POST /api/decisions within the supplied product intent and API contract. Stay inside the contract.

docs.title: The contract
docs.text:
Input Rule title Required non-empty string; duplicate check ignores case context Required non-empty string decision Required non-empty string status proposed, accepted, or superseded

Generate an ID and UTC timestamp. Keep state in memory.

Package tested source in a non-root runtime image with production dependencies and a health check.

docs.title: Fast checks that find weak work
docs.text:
1. Send a required field as whitespace or a number.
  2. Create the same trimmed title with different case.
  3. Send malformed JSON.
  4. Inspect the exact error envelope.
  5. Check which stage supplies source to the runtime image.

These checks test invalid inputs and container build boundaries.

docs.title: Keep the handoff short
docs.text: challenge-handoff.md holds the four file paths, your decision, open risks, and the next action. Don't copy phase text or command output into it.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M5-03 lab: HVE from product intent to reviewed code
docs.text:
Duration: 3 hours

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: HVE Core installed; Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04 and M3-04 or equivalent experience

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Use HVE Core to take one Engineering Decision API feature through the four RPI phases: Research, Plan, Implement, Review. Customizing HVE for the repository and using the product agents are optional and fit only if you finish the core exercises early.

The handoff is an index of the HVE artifacts and your decision.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• RPI: Research, Plan, Implement, Review. Four phases, each run by its own prompt. A fifth step, Follow-up, sends defects, decision gaps, and evidence gaps back to the phase that owns them.
  • File as interface: each phase writes a Markdown file under .copilot-tracking/. The next phase reads that file, not the chat. You can read it, diff it, edit it, and attach it to a fresh chat.
  • BRD / PRD: business requirements document (why the business wants this) and product requirements document (what the product must do). @BRD Builder and @PRD Builder write them. You use them when you start from a business idea. This lab starts from starter/product-intent.md.
  • applyTo glob: a frontmatter line in an .instructions.md file, such as applyTo: "src/**/*.js". The instruction loads only when Copilot works on a file that matches the pattern.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need Node.js 20 or later, GitHub Copilot, and the HVE Core extension or Copilot CLI plugin. Use synthetic decision records.

HVE command names and output paths change between versions. Check the HVE Core README and its RPI docs for your installed version. This lab uses the names below. If yours differ, use yours.

  1. Check that /rpi-research, /rpi-plan, /rpi-implement, /rpi-review, and /rpi are available. For the optional exercises, also check @Product Manager Advisor and @Agile Coach. Current HVE Core main replaced these agents with skills (requirements-author and the backlog skills), so use whatever your install offers. Type the command in chat. If it appears in the picker or runs, it's available. In Copilot CLI, /skills and /agent list what's loaded.
  2. Check that .copilot-tracking/ is ignored by Git.
  3. Run npm test (run npm ci first if dependencies are missing).
  4. Read starter/product-intent.md, starter/challenge-brief.md, and the artifact index in starter/challenge-handoff.md.
  5. Reserve the last 20 to 30 minutes for Review, your decision, and the handoff.

The baseline is one passing health test and no POST /api/decisions. If one HVE invocation fails, use starter/hve-phase-recovery.md and continue with the next phase.

docs.title: Pacing
docs.text:
Agent latency varies. Move on when the stage's files exist.

Stage Range Done when Preflight 10 to 15 min Commands are available and you can name the four tracking paths Research and Plan 30 to 40 min Research, plan, critique, and your approval exist Implement and validate 35 to 45 min Changes log, code, and test and container results exist Review and combined-RPI comparison 20 to 30 min Review file, your decision, and the comparison note exist Optional: customization 20 to 25 min You can name one change a repository file caused Optional: product and Agile agents 20 to 25 min You have a story, criteria, and exclusions

The required stages take about 1 hour 35 minutes to 2 hours 10 minutes. Do the optional stages with the time that remains, between Plan and Implement.

docs.title: Exercise 1: Run Research and Plan
docs.text:
Four kinds of file drive HVE: agents (roles), prompts (slash-command entry points), instructions (standards by file pattern), and .copilot-tracking/ files (state between phases).

Run:

/rpi-research "Add POST /api/decisions to the starter API using the supplied product intent and feature contract"

Expect a file like .copilot-tracking/research/<date>/<task>-research.md. Open it. It should record the scope, a rejected alternative, a constraint, and the next phase.

Clear the chat, attach the research file, then run /rpi-plan. Expect a plan under .copilot-tracking/plans/<date>/ and a plan critique under .copilot-tracking/reviews/plans/<date>/. Read both. Approve the plan only when every acceptance criterion maps to an owning file and a focused check.

docs.title: Optional exercise 2: Customize HVE for the repository
docs.text:
Create three repository-owned files:

  1. .github/copilot-instructions.md with the service context, architecture, data boundary, and dependency rule. Copilot loads it for every request in the repository.
  2. .github/instructions/javascript-api.instructions.md with description and applyTo frontmatter for src/**/*.js and tests/**/*.test.js. Require stable envelopes, app-instance state, and HTTP-level tests.
  3. .github/agents/decision-api-reviewer.agent.md with a narrow review mission, read/search tools only, and a response format that maps findings to criteria.

Check that each one is active:

File How to check copilot-instructions.md Ask "What rules does this repository give you?" The answer should quote it. In VS Code, the response's References list shows the file. *.instructions.md Open or edit a file that matches applyTo, then ask a question about it. The instruction should appear in References. A file outside the glob should not load it. *.agent.md The agent appears in the agent picker (/agent in Copilot CLI). Run it once and check its answer uses your response format.

Then re-run /rpi-plan or review the plan again, and note one concrete change caused by one of the files. Creating a file alone doesn't show HVE used it.

docs.title: Optional exercise 3: Product and Agile agents
docs.text:
Give starter/product-intent.md to @Product Manager Advisor. Ask it to test the feature's value, users, assumptions, priority, and non-goals. Cite its output from the plan.

Give the advisor output and starter/challenge-brief.md to @Agile Coach. Ask for one outcome-oriented user story, acceptance criteria, and named exclusions. Compare those criteria with the plan. Update the plan if they expose a gap, and say so in the plan. Don't create live work items.

Use the agent picker to find @BRD Builder and @PRD Builder. Write one sentence on when you'd start with each instead of product-intent.md.

docs.title: Exercise 4: Implement and review
docs.text:
Attach the approved plan (and any product or Agile output), then run /rpi-implement. The finished behavior must:

  • require non-empty string values for title, context, and decision;
  • accept proposed, accepted, or superseded as status;
  • default status to proposed;
  • reject a stored title after trimmed, case-insensitive comparison;
  • generate a unique string ID and UTC createdAt value;
  • return stable success and error envelopes;
  • keep the health route test passing;
  • run tests in a container build stage;
  • ship only production dependencies and tested source in the runtime stage;
  • run as a non-root user with a health check for GET /health.

Expect a changes log under .copilot-tracking/changes/<date>/. Then run /rpi-review and expect a review file under .copilot-tracking/reviews/logs/<date>/. Review every criterion as pass, fail, deferred, or not run. Check that errors reveal no stack traces, app instances do not share records, and the runtime image excludes development dependencies and root execution.

If the platform produces commit or pull-request text, leave it in the platform output. Don't commit, push, merge, or create a remote pull request.

docs.title: Compare direct and combined RPI
docs.text:
You just ran the phases one at a time. Don't start a second feature. Write a short note, using the table:

Direct prompts (what you ran) Combined /rpi task="..." You type One prompt per phase One prompt for the task Approval You approve between phases Depends on the mode you pick. Some modes check in; some run end to end Files you get One file per phase, at the paths above The same kinds of files, tied to one task name. Some versions also open a workflow canvas After Review You decide where defects go Follow-up routes defects to Implement, decision gaps to Plan, and evidence gaps to Research Use it when Learning, demos, explicit approvals You trust the handoffs

In your note, say which defect or gap from your own Review Follow-up would send back, and to which phase.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Fill in starter/challenge-handoff.md:

  • the paths of the four phase files;
  • your decision (approve, request changes, or pause);
  • open risks and the next action.

If you did the optional exercises, add the paths of the repository files and the agent outputs. Keep test and container results in the Implement or Review file.

docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Use the API challenge to teach how HVE works. Learners run Research, Plan, Implement, and Review and read the file each phase writes. Customization and the product agents are optional, so the 3-hour lab fits.

docs.title: Pacing
docs.text:
Model response time and questions change the pace. Shorten demonstrations before you cut artifact review.

Segment Range What learners should show What HVE is, RPI, and file as interface 8 to 12 min They can say what R, P, I, R stand for and why phases hand off through files Direct RPI phases and their handoffs 15 to 20 min Each phase has an owner, a file, and a gate Direct vs combined /rpi, Follow-up 5 to 10 min They can choose direct prompts or combined mode Optional: customization and applyTo 5 to 8 min They can check that an instruction, agent, or prompt is active Optional: product and Agile agents, BRD and PRD 5 to 8 min They can place Advisor, Coach, BRD, and PRD before RPI Challenge handoff 2 to 4 min They know which files to fill in

If an agent response is slow, switch to the reference artifact and keep talking.

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• Install Node.js 20 or later and the HVE Core extension or Copilot CLI plugin. Open Copilot Chat and check the RPI prompts and agents appear.
  • HVE Core releases often and command names, docs, and output paths move. This session's names (/rpi-research, /rpi-plan, /rpi-implement, /rpi-review, Follow-up, .copilot-tracking/reviews/logs/) match the main docs checked on 12 November 2026. The plugin follows main. The latest tagged release, v3.2.2 (March 2026), uses older names. Install the version you teach, read its docs, and run the demo once. Adjust names in the slides and lab if they differ.
  • On main, Product Manager Advisor and Agile Coach are no longer agents. Their questioning and story-quality guidance moved into the requirements-author and backlog skills. If your install has no such agents, run optional exercise 3 through those skills or demonstrate it.
  • A clean copy of the starter.
  • Reference RPI artifacts and product and Agile outputs.
  • Captured test output and container-build result.
  • One trainer-provided artifact per RPI phase, in case an invocation fails.

Generic agent mode doesn't replace an HVE phase. Without HVE, run an instructor walkthrough. Learners can inspect the artifacts but can't complete the challenge.

docs.title: Teach HVE first
docs.text:
HVE is a structured engineering framework for GitHub Copilot. RPI is its core workflow: Research, Plan, Implement, Review, then Follow-up. Learners must distinguish four parts:

  • agents own roles and protocols;
  • prompts provide repeatable workflow entry points;
  • instructions apply standards when file patterns match;
  • .copilot-tracking/ stores local handoff files between phases and stays ignored by Git.

File as interface means the next phase reads the previous phase's file, not the chat. Open the file Research writes for Plan. Show how a person reads it, diffs it, edits it, attaches it to a fresh chat, and approves it.

docs.title: Demonstrate direct RPI phases
docs.text:
Use the starter product intent and run the first two phases live:

/rpi-research "Add POST /api/decisions using the supplied product intent and feature contract"
/rpi-plan

Pause on the artifacts, not the chat narration.

Phase Question Output Research What do we know, what limits apply, and what is uncertain? Research findings and alternatives Plan What will change, in what order, and which checks will catch mistakes? Plan and critique Implement Did the changes follow the approved plan? Code, tests, and changes log Review Does the result satisfy the request and quality bar? Findings, criterion verdicts, decision

Expected files, with <date> and <task> filled in by HVE:

.copilot-tracking/research/<date>/<task>-research.md
.copilot-tracking/plans/<date>/<task>-plan.md
.copilot-tracking/reviews/plans/<date>/<task>-plan-critique.md
.copilot-tracking/changes/<date>/<task>-changes.md
.copilot-tracking/reviews/logs/<date>/<task>-review.md

Then show the combined form without running a second feature:

/rpi task="<bounded task>"

Combined RPI writes the same kinds of files under one task name, and the mode you pick decides how often it stops for your approval. After Review, Follow-up routes defects to Implement, decision gaps to Plan, and evidence gaps to Research. Use direct prompts to learn and approve phase by phase. Use combined mode once the team trusts the workflow. Check your version's docs for exact prompt syntax and modes.

docs.title: Demonstrate customization (optional)
docs.text:
Show these files in the reference project:

.github/copilot-instructions.md
.github/instructions/javascript-api.instructions.md
.github/agents/decision-api-reviewer.agent.md

HVE is additive. Repository context reaches every agent. Targeted instructions activate only for matching files. A custom agent adds a role with its own mission, tools, protocol, and output contract.

An instruction's frontmatter has an applyTo glob, for example applyTo: "src/**/*.js". Copilot loads the instruction only for matching files.

Show how to check each piece is active:

  • Instruction: edit a matching file, ask a question, and look for the instruction in the response's References. Repeat with a non-matching file.
  • Agent: find it in the agent picker (/agent in Copilot CLI) and run it once.
  • Prompt: type / and the name. It appears in the picker and runs.

Ask learners what changed in Research, Plan, code, or Review. Creating a file doesn't show it was used.

docs.title: Demonstrate the product-to-engineering handoff (optional)
docs.text:
Business idea
  → @BRD Builder or supplied product intent
  → @Product Manager Advisor
  → @PRD Builder when a full product specification is needed
  → @Agile Coach
  → approved HVE plan
  → Implement and Review

A BRD says why the business wants the thing. A PRD says what the product must do. Learners start with supplied intent, use Product Manager Advisor to test value and assumptions, then use Agile Coach to produce one story and acceptance criteria. They update the HVE plan when those outputs expose a gap. The Plan artifact cites the outputs. Learners don't copy them into the handoff. No live backlog writes.

docs.title: Reference demonstration
docs.text: Show one valid create request, a duplicate whose title uses different case, and a malformed JSON response. Then show the test and runtime stages in the Dockerfile. Keep the RPI artifact chain open beside the code so learners can trace the implementation back to product and Agile decisions.

docs.title: Coaching prompts
docs.text:
• Which file controls the behavior you need to change?
  • Which HVE phase owns that decision?
  • What check could disprove your plan fastest?
  • Which acceptance criterion lacks test results?
  • Does the image build test the exact source copied into the runtime stage?
  • Did an instruction change the review, or did you only create the file?
  • Did Product Manager Advisor or Agile Coach change the plan?
  • What would make you pause rather than approve?

docs.title: Reviewing results
docs.text:
Look for each file at its generated path. lab/solution/reference-notes.md lists where. Check that the handoff has the four paths, the learner's decision, open risks, and the next action, not copied phase text.

The learner ends with a decision: approve, request changes, or pause. If a phase failed and you supplied a recovery file, the learner says so in the handoff.

docs.title: Session M6-01: Build reliable agent applications with the GitHub Copilot SDK
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Module 6: Advanced Topics & Capstone

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04, M3-01 to M3-05

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content, 2 hour lab)

SDK version: @github/copilot-sdk 1.0.16, pinned in the starter and solution

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Build a TypeScript CLI around an agent to assess whether a synthetic software change is ready to proceed.

You write the reliability controls in application code. The CLI manages the client and session lifecycle, streams progress, and limits tool use. It also shows denied actions, records failures, and closes resources. Tests check that control path. An optional extension sends traces through an OpenTelemetry Collector to Jaeger.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• manage CopilotClient and session startup, use, and shutdown;
  • subscribe to streaming session events without printing duplicate final output;
  • define a typed custom tool over deterministic synthetic data;
  • separate tool availability, permission handling, and pre-tool policy;
  • use pre-tool, failed-tool, error, and session-end hooks;
  • make a denied action visible to the user and trace;
  • test the allowed, denied, failed, and cleanup paths;
  • tell what the SDK provides from what the sample app chooses;
  • (optional) send SDK traces through an OpenTelemetry Collector to Jaeger.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text: Learners need authenticated GitHub Copilot SDK access, Node.js and npm, and a terminal. The optional tracing extension also needs Docker with Docker Compose.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
The application is a change readiness assistant. It reads deterministic synthetic change records, asks Copilot to assess the selected change, and returns ready or needs-review with the supporting gaps.

One request targets a restricted synthetic record. The application denies that lookup before execution and shows the reason.

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Content Trainer content 60 min Slides, concepts, and prepared demo Lab 120 min Build and check the CLI

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab guide lab/README.md Starter project lab/starter/sdk-readiness-assistant/ Reference solution lab/solution/sdk-readiness-assistant/

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The lab covers:

  • local CopilotClient and session lifecycle;
  • TypeScript streaming event handlers;
  • one application-owned readiness tool;
  • recorded permission decisions;
  • pre-tool, post-tool-failure, error, and session-end hooks;
  • a visible denied action;
  • focused automated tests;
  • optional extension: OTLP export through an OpenTelemetry Collector and trace inspection in Jaeger.

The session doesn't cover dynamic workflows, fleet, cloud or remote sessions, BYOK, plugin packaging, production deployment, external business systems, or other languages.

docs.title: Build reliable agent applications with the GitHub Copilot SDK
docs.text:
Own the lifecycle, policy, run records, and failure path

Session M6-01 | Module 6 | Advanced

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time The application reliability boundary 10 min Client, session, and streaming lifecycle 12 min Tools, permissions, and hooks 17 min Tests 8 min Prepared demo and lab handoff 13 min

docs.title: The application owns the control path
docs.text:
The SDK provides an agent session. Your application still owns:

  • startup and shutdown;
  • the data boundary;
  • which tools exist;
  • which calls may run;
  • what the user sees when work fails;
  • the records kept after the session ends.

A useful answer with an unsafe control path is still a broken application.

docs.title: What the SDK guarantees and what this sample chooses
docs.text:
The SDK provides This sample chooses Client, session, event, and hook APIs One session, cleanup in finally Event name assistant.message_delta Print deltas only Hook names and return shapes What each hook records Permission result kinds Approve only lookup_change_request onPostToolUseFailure skips denied calls Treat denial as policy, not error

The package is @github/copilot-sdk, pinned to 1.0.16 (latest on npm: 1.0.31). If you upgrade, add "types": ["node"] to tsconfig.json and check the SDK release notes.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
• assistant.message_delta: a piece of the streamed reply. Deltas "CR-10", "42 is ", "ready." print as CR-1042 is ready.
  • Hook: a function the SDK calls at a fixed point in a session.
  • Hook return shape: the fields a hook may return, for example { permissionDecision: "deny", permissionDecisionReason: "..." }.
  • OTLP: the wire format OpenTelemetry uses to send traces.
  • Span: one timed step in a trace, such as a tool call.

docs.title: The scenario is deliberately small
docs.text:
Synthetic change record
        ↓
TypeScript CLI
        ↓
Copilot session
        ↓
Change request lookup tool
        ↓
ready or needs-review

The data is fixed. You build the controls around the model.

docs.title: Manage startup and cleanup
docs.text:
import { CopilotClient } from "@github/copilot-sdk";

const client = new CopilotClient({
  telemetry: { otlpEndpoint: "http://localhost:4318" },
});

await client.start();
let session;

try {
  session = await client.createSession(config);
  await session.sendAndWait({ prompt });
} finally {
  await session?.disconnect();
  await client.stop();
}

Cleanup belongs in finally.

docs.title: One client can own several sessions
docs.text:
Object Owns Close when CopilotClient Runtime connection and client options The application exits Session Conversation state, tools, hooks, and events The task is complete Event subscription UI updates from that session The session is no longer observed Collector connection (optional) Trace export path The local trace stack stops

Keep session state scoped by session ID. Remove it in the session-end path.

docs.title: Streaming improves feedback and creates edge cases
docs.text:
session.on("assistant.message_delta", (event) => {
  if (!event.agentId) {
    process.stdout.write(event.data.deltaContent);
  }
});

session.on("session.idle", () => {
  process.stdout.write("\n");
});

The final assistant.message still arrives. Decide whether the CLI renders deltas, the final message, or both in different places. Printing both produces duplicates.

docs.title: Events do not decide readiness
docs.text:
Session events can show:

  • text deltas;
  • tool requests and results;
  • permission requests;
  • session state changes;
  • usage records.

The readiness verdict must still come from the application's deterministic data and rules. Do not infer readiness from a fluent answer.

docs.title: A custom tool limits what the agent can do
docs.text:
import { defineTool } from "@github/copilot-sdk";

const lookupTool = defineTool("lookup_change_request", {
  description: "Read one synthetic change and calculate readiness gaps",
  parameters: {
    type: "object",
    properties: { requestId: { type: "string" } },
    required: ["requestId"],
    additionalProperties: false,
  },
  handler: async (args) => lookupChangeRequest(changes, args),
});

The schema narrows the input. The handler still validates the request ID before it reads the fixture.

docs.title: Tool availability and permission answer different questions
docs.text:
Control Question Registered tools Can the model choose this capability? onPermissionRequest May this requested execution proceed? onPreToolUse Does application policy allow these exact arguments now? Tool handler Are the input and data valid at execution time?

Use all four where the risk justifies them. One broad approval does not replace argument-level policy.

docs.title: Deny the action before the handler runs
docs.text:
hooks: {
  onPreToolUse: async (input) => {
    if (
      input.toolName === "lookup_change_request" &&
      input.toolArgs?.requestId?.startsWith("RESTRICTED-")
    ) {
      return {
        permissionDecision: "deny",
        permissionDecisionReason:
          "Restricted change requests cannot be read by this assistant.",
      };
    }

    return { permissionDecision: "allow" };
  },
}

The denial reason should appear in the CLI and trace. Silent denial is hard to debug and easy to misread.

docs.title: Keep permission handling narrow
docs.text:
onPermissionRequest: async (request) => {
  if ("managedApprovalRequired" in request &&
      request.managedApprovalRequired === true) {
    return { kind: "no-result" };
  }

  if ("toolName" in request &&
      request.toolName === "lookup_change_request") {
    return { kind: "approve-once" };
  }

  return {
    kind: "reject",
    feedback: "Only the synthetic readiness tool is allowed.",
  };
},

Deny unknown request kinds. Review new capabilities before approving them so they do not inherit permission by accident.

docs.title: Hooks record and control the lifecycle
docs.text:
Session starts
  → request streams
  → tool call reaches pre-tool policy
  → permission decision
  → handler succeeds or fails
  → failure or error hook records the outcome
  → session ends and state is cleared

Hooks run inline. Keep them fast and deterministic.

docs.title: Failure and error are different paths
docs.text:
Path Example Application response Denied call Restricted synthetic ID violates policy Show the reason, record denial Application result Malformed or missing synthetic ID Return a fixed result without invention Tool execution failure Handler throws or returns a failed execution Record the failed tool event SDK error Runtime or model call fails Notify the user, retry only when safe Session end Complete, abort, timeout, or error Flush state and record reason

Do not turn every failure into a retry. Some failures are policy decisions.

docs.title: Use the failed-tool hook for agent guidance
docs.text:
onPostToolUseFailure: async (input) => {
  audit.failedTools.push({
    toolName: input.toolName,
    error: input.error,
  });

  return {
    additionalContext:
      "Do not invent a change record. Report the failed tool result.",
  };
},

This hook sees failed tool results only. It does not fire for denied calls and does not replace onErrorOccurred.

docs.title: Use the error hook for SDK recovery policy
docs.text:
onErrorOccurred: async (input) => {
  audit.errors.push(input.error);

  return {
    errorHandling: input.recoverable ? "retry" : "abort",
    retryCount: input.recoverable ? 1 : 0,
    userNotification: "The readiness session could not continue.",
  };
},

Retry once only when the error says recovery is possible. Keep the original error in the audit record.

docs.title: End every session with a record
docs.text:
onSessionEnd: async (input, invocation) => {
  audit.endReason = input.reason;
  audit.endedAt = new Date().toISOString();
  sessionState.delete(invocation.sessionId);

  return {
    sessionSummary: `Readiness session ended: ${input.reason}`,
  };
},

Cleanup should be safe to run more than once. A process crash may skip the hook, so the outer finally block still matters.

docs.title: Test the control path, not model phrasing
docs.text:
Test Stable assertion CR-1042 Tool returns ready with no gaps CR-2087 Tool returns needs-review with fixed gaps Restricted ID Pre-tool hook returns deny with the required reason Failed tool event Failed-tool hook records the failure SDK error Error hook chooses the expected recovery action Session completion End hook clears state and records the reason Streaming Deltas render once and final output is not duplicated

Mock the SDK boundary. Keep synthetic data fixed.

docs.title: Optional extension: trace the run outside the terminal
docs.text:
CLI process
   │ OTLP/HTTP :4318
   ▼
OpenTelemetry Collector
   │ OTLP
   ▼
Jaeger :16686

const client = new CopilotClient({
  telemetry: {
    otlpEndpoint: "http://localhost:4318",
  },
});

The trace should show session work, tool activity, the denied action, and the end reason for one run.

docs.title: Optional extension: inspect the run in Jaeger
docs.text:
Use Jaeger to check:

  • which span contained the tool request;
  • whether the denied action reached the handler;
  • how long the model and tool steps took;
  • where a failed run stopped;
  • whether one CLI invocation produced one connected trace.

Trace data can contain prompts and tool details. Keep this lab synthetic.

docs.title: Reliability has tradeoffs
docs.text:
Choice Benefit Cost Stream deltas Faster visible feedback More rendering state Deny by default Smaller execution boundary More permission code Hooks for audit One lifecycle view Inline latency if hooks do too much Deterministic tool data Stable tests and demos Less realism Local tracing stack (optional) Traces you can inspect Docker setup and local resource use

Choose controls that show what failed and why.

docs.title: Prepared demonstration
docs.text:
1. Run the passing tests.
  2. Assess a known synthetic change.
  3. Watch the response stream.
  4. Request the restricted synthetic record.
  5. Show the denial in the terminal.
  6. Trigger an unknown ID and show the failure path.
  7. Optional: open the same run in Jaeger.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Build the CLI in lab/starter/sdk-readiness-assistant/.

You will complete the lifecycle, streaming, readiness tool, permissions, hooks, and tests. Then you will run the known, denied, and failed paths. Tracing in Jaeger is an optional extension.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M6-01 lab: Build a change readiness assistant
docs.text: Duration: 120 minutes Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04, M3-01 to M3-05 and the Session M6-01 trainer content

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Complete a TypeScript CLI that uses the GitHub Copilot SDK to assess synthetic change records. The CLI streams the response, calls one readiness tool, denies a restricted lookup, records failures, and passes focused tests.

Tracing with Docker Compose, an OpenTelemetry Collector, and Jaeger is an optional extension after the core lab.

docs.title: What the SDK does and what this sample chooses
docs.text:
Keep these apart. You change the second column; you can't change the first.

The SDK provides This sample chooses CopilotClient, sessions, sendAndWait, disconnect, stop One client, one session, cleanup in finally The event name assistant.message_delta and the agentId field Print only deltas with no agentId, and keep the final message for records Hook names: onPreToolUse, onPostToolUseFailure, onErrorOccurred, onSessionEnd What each hook records and returns Hook return shapes (see the glossary) Deny RESTRICTED- IDs; retry once on a recoverable error onPermissionRequest and the result kinds approve-once and reject Approve only lookup_change_request onPostToolUseFailure fires only for failed tool results, not for denied calls Treat a denial as a policy result, not an error A telemetry client option Endpoint, source name, and captureContent: false

The SDK is @github/copilot-sdk, pinned to 1.0.16 in package.json and the lock file. That is the version this lab was tested with end to end. On 12 November 2026 the latest version on npm was 1.0.31. The offline build and unit tests also pass on 1.0.31 if you add "types": ["node"] to tsconfig.json; the live demo wasn't run on it. If you upgrade, add that line and check the SDK release notes for hook and event changes.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning Example assistant.message_delta A session event carrying a small piece of the streamed reply. The final assistant.message event carries the whole reply. Deltas "CR-10", "42 is ", "ready." print as CR-1042 is ready. The final message repeats the same text, so don't print it too. Hook A function the SDK calls at a fixed point in a session. It can record, change, or block what happens next. onPreToolUse runs before a tool handler. Hook return shape The object a hook returns. Each hook accepts different fields. Pre-tool: { permissionDecision: "deny", permissionDecisionReason: "..." }. Failed tool: { additionalContext: "..." }. Error: { errorHandling: "retry", retryCount: 1 }. Session end: { sessionSummary: "..." }. OTLP OpenTelemetry Protocol, the wire format for traces. Used only in the extension. The SDK sends OTLP over HTTP to http://localhost:4318. Span One timed step in a trace, such as a tool call. A trace is a tree of spans for one run. A lookup_change_request span sits under the session span. Synthetic data Fake records in fixtures/change-requests.json. No real systems or people. CR-1042, RESTRICTED-0001

docs.title: Final deliverables
docs.text:
Demonstrate:

  1. a working CLI under sdk-readiness-assistant/;
  2. client and session cleanup on success and on thrown errors;
  3. streamed output printed once;
  4. the typed readiness tool over the synthetic data;
  5. a permission handler and pre-tool policy that deny RESTRICTED-0001 with a visible reason;
  6. failed-tool, error, and session-end hook records;
  7. passing tests and type checks.

docs.title: Time plan
docs.text: Part Work Time Setup Install and baseline 15 min 1 Client, session, and streaming 25 min 2 Readiness tool and policy 30 min 3 Failure hooks and cleanup 25 min 4 Tests and final run 25 min Extension Jaeger tracing (optional) 20 min

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Work from:

sessions/session-m6-01-copilot-sdk/lab/starter/sdk-readiness-assistant/

You need authenticated GitHub Copilot, and Node.js and npm at the versions in package.json. Use Copilot authentication, not BYOK or another provider. Docker is only for the extension.

node --version
npm --version
npm ci
npm run check
npm test

Some tests should fail. They are your baseline: each failing test marks a control you will add. The project still compiles. The authentication check in src/live-demo.ts runs before the live demo.

Project files you will touch:

src/live-demo.ts          client, session, streaming, hooks
src/change-store.ts       lookup over fixtures/change-requests.json
src/permission-policy.ts  permission decisions
src/hook-decisions.ts     pre-tool, failure, error, and end decisions
tests/                    one test file per module

Don't add data sources or runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Part 1: Lifecycle and streaming (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Start the client, create one session, stream parent-agent output, and close everything on every exit path.

  1. Create CopilotClient and call client.start() before creating the session.
  2. Create one session with streaming: true.
  3. Subscribe to assistant.message_delta. Print only deltas with no agentId.
  4. Keep the final message for tests. Don't print it again.
  5. Put session.disconnect() and client.stop() in finally.
  6. Key per-session state by session ID.
const client = new CopilotClient(clientOptions);
await client.start();
let session;

try {
  session = await client.createSession(sessionConfig);
  subscribeToOutput(session);
  await session.sendAndWait({ prompt });
} finally {
  await session?.disconnect();
  await client.stop();
}

npm run check
npm test

Checkpoint 1. The session and client close after success and after a thrown error. Parent text prints once. Session state isn't global.

docs.title: Part 2: Readiness tool and policy (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Expose the synthetic data through one typed tool. Allow normal lookups. Deny the restricted record before the handler runs.

  1. Don't edit the record IDs or verdicts in fixtures/change-requests.json.
  2. Complete the lookup_change_request tool and its JSON Schema.
  3. Validate the ID inside the handler. Return the fixed invalid-input or not-found result for bad IDs.
  4. In onPermissionRequest, approve only the readiness tool and reject everything else. Don't use an approve-all helper.
  5. In onPreToolUse, deny IDs that start with RESTRICTED- with this reason:
Restricted change requests cannot be read by this assistant.
  1. Record whether the handler ran. The denial test must show it didn't.
npm test

Checkpoint 2.

  • CR-1042 returns ready with no gaps.
  • CR-2087 returns needs-review with fixed gaps.
  • Malformed and unknown IDs return fixed results.
  • RESTRICTED-0001 is denied with the reason above, and the handler never runs.

docs.title: Part 3: Failure, error, and end hooks (25 minutes)
docs.text:
1. onPostToolUseFailure: record the tool name and error. Return additionalContext telling the agent to report unknown data, not invent a record.
  2. onErrorOccurred: store the original error. Retry once if the SDK marks it recoverable. Otherwise abort with a short userNotification.
  3. onSessionEnd: record the reason and time, and delete that session's state. Make it safe to call twice.

A denied tool call isn't an SDK error. It's a policy result, and it doesn't trigger onPostToolUseFailure.

npm test
npm run check

Checkpoint 3. The audit record separates a policy denial, a failed tool, a recoverable or unrecoverable error, and the session end reason. Session state is empty after the end hook.

docs.title: Part 4: Tests and final run (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Test the control path, not the model's wording. Mock the SDK at the boundaries the starter provides. Don't call a live model from unit tests.

Complete the tests so they cover:

  • known ready and blocked changes, and malformed and unknown IDs;
  • the denied RESTRICTED-0001 lookup, and that the handler didn't run;
  • one retry for a recoverable error, and abort for an unrecoverable one;
  • session state cleanup;
  • deltas rendered once;
  • client shutdown after an exception.
npm test
npm run check
npm run lint   # only if package.json defines it

Then run the live demo:

npm run demo

Final checkpoint. Tests pass twice with no data or snapshot changes. In the demo, CR-1042 streams a ready assessment, bad-id returns the fixed invalid-input result, RESTRICTED-0001 prints the denial reason, and the session and client close.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix client.getAuthStatus() reports unauthenticated Check the GitHub Copilot sign-in and network. Session creation fails Check the lock file, Node.js version, and Copilot access. Output is duplicated Print deltas only. Keep the final message for records. Restricted data reaches the handler Match the exact tool name and check toolArgs.requestId in onPreToolUse. Unknown IDs produce an invented answer Return a failed tool result and add failure-hook context that forbids invention. Tests call the live model Mock the session boundary. Session state remains Delete the session ID in onSessionEnd.

docs.title: Solution reference
docs.text: Compare your work with lab/solution/sdk-readiness-assistant/: src/live-demo.ts, src/change-store.ts, src/permission-policy.ts, src/hook-decisions.ts, and tests/.

docs.title: Optional extension: trace the run in Jaeger
docs.text:
Do this after the core lab. It adds Docker Compose, an OpenTelemetry Collector, and Jaeger so you can see the same run as a trace. It needs Docker with Docker Compose and free local ports.

The SDK sends OTLP (the OpenTelemetry wire format) over HTTP to the Collector on port 4318. The Collector forwards spans to Jaeger.

CLI → OTLP/HTTP :4318 → OpenTelemetry Collector → Jaeger :16686
  1. Read compose.yaml and otel-collector-config.yaml.
  2. Check docker version and docker compose version.
  3. Start the stack and wait until both services are healthy:
docker compose -f compose.yaml up -d
docker compose -f compose.yaml ps
  1. Run npm run demo.
  2. Open http://localhost:16686, select the project's service name, and find the three most recent traces.
  3. In the RESTRICTED-0001 trace, check that no handler span follows the denial.
  4. Find the permitted and invalid-input traces.
  5. Stop the stack:
docker compose -f compose.yaml down
Problem Fix Collector can't bind port 4318 Stop the process that uses it, or change the port in both config files. Jaeger is empty Check container health, the Collector pipeline, the service name, and the time range.

Duration: 60 minutes Format: Concept teaching, prepared live demo, lab briefing

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Show where the model's work ends and application code takes over. The model produces an assessment. TypeScript code manages the lifecycle, limits tools, makes permission decisions, and handles failures. Tracing is an optional extension.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text:
Time Segment What learners should show 0:00 to 0:10 Application reliability boundary, SDK guarantees vs sample choices, glossary They can name what the application owns and what the SDK provides 0:10 to 0:22 Client, session, and streaming They can draw the startup and cleanup path 0:22 to 0:39 Tool, permissions, and hooks They can explain where a call is denied and what each hook returns 0:39 to 0:47 Tests They can name a stable assertion for each path 0:47 to 0:57 Prepared live demo The denied action is visible in the CLI 0:57 to 1:00 Lab transition Every learner has the tools installed

Use slides.md for the teaching sequence.

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
1. Install Node.js and npm at the versions the project declares.
  2. Optional: check that Docker Compose starts the supplied local stack.
  3. Sign in to GitHub Copilot with the account learners will use.
  4. In the reference solution, run npm ci, the tests, and the type check.
  5. Run one successful assessment.
  6. Run the denied action and check the reason appears in the terminal.
  7. Optional: start the OpenTelemetry Collector and Jaeger, and find both runs as traces.
  8. Keep the solution project open at the demo files.

docs.title: What the SDK guarantees and what the sample chooses
docs.text:
Use the table in the slides and the lab. The SDK defines the API: event names, hook names and return shapes, permission result kinds. The sample defines the policy: the tool name, the RESTRICTED- rule, the retry count, and the allow-list. If a learner changes a policy value, tests change. If they change an SDK name, the code stops compiling. The lab pins @github/copilot-sdk 1.0.16. For 1.0.31 (latest on 12 November 2026), add "types": ["node"] to tsconfig.json and check the SDK release notes.

Cover the glossary in the lab README before the streaming segment: delta, hook return shape, OTLP, span. Skip OTLP and span unless you teach the extension.

docs.title: The application owns the boundary
docs.text:
Open with the synthetic change record. Ask which parts need model reasoning and which should stay deterministic.

The readiness tool returns fixed lookup results. The model can explain them, but it can't create a record or change the policy. That separation makes the lab testable.

  • register only lookup_change_request;
  • inspect exact tool arguments before execution;
  • deny unrecognized permission requests;
  • show policy denial to the user;
  • clean up even when the session fails.

docs.title: Client and session lifecycle
docs.text:
construct client → start client → create session → subscribe →
send request → await completion → close session state → stop client

The session-end hook records what the agent runtime reports. The outer finally block handles process-level cleanup. You need both.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
Show assistant.message_delta and the final assistant.message as separate event types. A CLI that prints both as primary output repeats the response.

The application streams parent-agent text deltas and uses complete events for records and tests. It ignores sub-agent output.

docs.title: Tool and permission layers
docs.text:
Registration, permission requests, pre-tool policy, and handler validation are separate controls. Use the table from the slides.

The lookup tool accepts one synthetic request ID. Normal CR-#### values reach the handler. IDs beginning with RESTRICTED- test the denial path. The pre-tool hook blocks them before the handler runs.

docs.title: Failure and error hooks
docs.text:
• malformed input returns a fixed validation result;
  • a failed tool execution enters onPostToolUseFailure;
  • a runtime or model error enters onErrorOccurred.

A policy denial is not an error. The application did what it was designed to do.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: The tests assert control decisions and deterministic results, not the model's prose.

docs.title: Optional extension: traces
docs.text: Jaeger shows the timing and sequence of a run: whether the restricted call reached the handler and where a failed run stopped. Trace payloads can expose prompts and tool arguments, so the lab uses synthetic data. Teach this only if time allows.

docs.title: Demo: a denied change request
docs.text:
Level: L300 Time: 10 minutes

Show the denied lookup for RESTRICTED-0001 in the terminal. If you set up the extension, open Jaeger and point to the same blocked tool call.

  1. Show the starting state. Open lab/solution/sdk-readiness-assistant/. Point to fixtures/change-requests.json, src/live-demo.ts, src/permission-policy.ts, src/hook-decisions.ts, and the tests.

"The model doesn't own this data or policy. TypeScript decides which capability exists and whether the exact call may run."

  1. Run the baseline.
npm test
npm run check

"I want the control path green before I involve a live model. These tests cover known data, denial, failure handling, streaming, and cleanup. They don't compare natural-language answers."

  1. Run a permitted assessment. Run npm run demo. The first request assesses CR-1042. Let the response stream. The renderer doesn't print the final event a second time.

  2. Watch the restricted lookup. The third prepared prompt requests RESTRICTED-0001. The tool is known, so the request reaches policy. The pre-tool hook checks the request ID and denies it before the handler runs.

  3. Point to the visible denial. Read the denial reason from the terminal and show the audit entry.

  4. Show invalid input and the failed-tool policy. Point to the bad-id run, then the failed-tool hook test and the session-end hook test. Invalid input returns a fixed validation result. A failed tool execution uses its own hook.

  5. Optional: show the trace. Start the stack with docker compose -f compose.yaml up -d, rerun npm run demo, and open Jaeger at http://localhost:16686. Select the project's service name. The latest trace shows the blocked tool call with no handler span after the denial.

  6. Close the demo. Stop the application.

docs.title: Demo troubleshooting
docs.text:
Problem Response SDK authentication fails Stop. Check the GitHub Copilot sign-in and network path. No streamed text appears Check the session enables streaming and the handler listens for parent assistant.message_delta events. Restricted data reaches the handler Stop. Check the exact tool name and parsed requestId in onPreToolUse, then rerun the denial test. Collector is unreachable (extension) Check Docker Compose health and the OTLP HTTP endpoint http://localhost:4318. Jaeger shows no trace (extension) Check the Collector exports to Jaeger, select the configured service name, and widen the time range. Output appears twice Check whether both message deltas and the final assistant message are printed as primary output.

Point learners to lab/README.md. They add the same controls to the starter project one layer at a time and run the focused checks at each checkpoint. Tracing is an optional extension at the end.

docs.text: Lab checkpoint Coach question Setup Did the install and the authenticated SDK call pass? Do the starter tests fail where expected? Lifecycle and streaming Where does cleanup run if sendAndWait throws? Tool and denial Do the test results show the handler did not run? Failure hooks Is unknown data reported without invention or broad retry? Tests Are assertions stable without matching model prose? Extension: traces Can the learner connect terminal output to one Jaeger trace?

docs.text:

Module: Advanced Topics & Capstone (Module 6)

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04, M3-01 to M3-05 and M5-02; Session M5-01 is optional

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content, 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Implement and review one Bookmark API slice: POST /api/bookmarks. You turn a supplied specification into a GitHub issue, prompt Copilot to implement it, and review the result against the spec and the tests. You finish with a handoff another engineer can use.

The capstone stays small on purpose. Authentication, persistent storage, deployment, and every other bookmark endpoint are out of scope. Use synthetic data and the existing dependencies.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Turn a specification into one implementation-ready issue.
  • Prompt Copilot to implement the issue.
  • Use the failing starter tests as the baseline.
  • Review the patch against the spec and the tests, not only the trace.
  • Hand off the result with a review decision and next action.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Starter files lab/starter/ Reference solution lab/solution/

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text: A reviewed handoff for POST /api/bookmarks with the issue, patch, test results, review decision, and next action.

docs.title: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text: Session M6-02 | 3 hours

docs.title: One slice
docs.text:
Implement and review:

POST /api/bookmarks

Everything else is deferred.

docs.title: The result is a handoff
docs.text:
• issue;
  • patch;
  • test results;
  • review decision and next action.

docs.title: Four terms
docs.text:
• Synthetic data: made-up bookmarks, such as https://docs.example.test/node.
  • Specification ID: the label of one requirement, such as FR-007.
  • Response envelope: success is { "data": ... }. Failure is { "error": { "code", "message" } }.
  • Baseline: test results before the change.

docs.title: The scope lives in the issue
docs.text: Implement only POST /api/bookmarks, use synthetic data, and keep the existing dependencies.

docs.title: Session M5-02 is an input
docs.text:
The accepted specification must separate:

Behavior Implementation constraint Observable request and response rules Node.js, Express, in-memory storage Validation and duplicate behavior Existing dependencies only Acceptance scenarios Exact files and test command

docs.title: Issue trace
docs.text:
Every acceptance criterion maps to:

specification ID -> planned file -> executable test

If the issue adds behavior missing from the specification, fix the issue first.

docs.title: Worked example: spec to issue to prompt
docs.text:
FR-007: a second request with the same URL returns 409.

Issue: Reject duplicate bookmark URLs
Specification IDs: FR-007, FR-008
Criterion: repeated url -> 409, error.code CONFLICT
Test: "rejects a duplicate URL"
Files: src/routes/bookmarks.js, src/models/bookmark.js

Implement this issue. Existing dependencies only. Don't edit tests/.
List the files and spec IDs first, then change, then run npm test.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In scope:

  • create one bookmark;
  • validate the accepted fields;
  • reject a duplicate URL;
  • return the documented envelope and status.

Out of scope: authentication, persistence, other endpoints, deployment, and new packages.

docs.title: The failing tests are the baseline
docs.text:
npm test

Health passes. The Bookmark tests fail because the route doesn't exist. They are the spec as executable checks. You're done when they pass. Don't edit them.

docs.title: Review and handover
docs.text:
Passing tests are where review starts.

  1. Run the suite.
  2. Check the diff: no edits under tests/, no new dependency.
  3. Name a test for each specification ID.
  4. Break a rule on purpose. The matching test must fail.
  5. Read the responses against the spec.
  6. Record the decision: approve or request changes.

docs.title: Lab time plan
docs.text: Phase Time Review the specification 15 min Write the issue and run the baseline 25 min Prompt Copilot to implement it 40 min Review, test, and hand off 40 min

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M6-02 lab: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04, M3-01 to M3-05 and M5-02; Session M5-01 is optional

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need repository or sandbox access, GitHub Copilot, Node.js 20 or later, a person to review your work, and synthetic bookmark data. Don't add a package or use production data. The only slice is POST /api/bookmarks.

Phase Work Time 1 Review the specification 15 min 2 Write the issue and run the baseline 25 min 3 Prompt Copilot to implement it 40 min 4 Review, test, and hand off 40 min

docs.title: Terms
docs.text: Term Meaning in this lab Synthetic data Made-up bookmarks such as https://docs.example.test/node. No real URLs, accounts, or user data. Specification ID The label of one requirement in starter/bookmark-create-spec.md, such as FR-007. Issues, patches, and tests cite these IDs. Response envelope The JSON wrapper around every response. Success is { "data": { ... } }. Failure is { "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }. Baseline The test results before you change anything: health passes, bookmark tests fail.

docs.title: Phase 1: Review the specification (15 min)
docs.text: Read starter/bookmark-create-spec.md once. Check that each requirement says something you can observe in a request or response, and that technology choices appear only under constraints. If a rule is ambiguous, ask your reviewer. Don't guess.

docs.title: Phase 2: Write the issue and run the baseline (25 min)
Worked example: from specification to issue
docs.text:
Take two requirements from the spec:

FR-007 A second request with the same URL returns 409 and does not create another bookmark. FR-008 Validation failures return 400 with error.code set to VALIDATION_ERROR. Duplicate URLs use CONFLICT.

An issue for the duplicate rule looks like this:

**Title:** Reject duplicate bookmark URLs on POST /api/bookmarks

**Goal:** A second POST with a URL that already exists returns 409 and stores
nothing new.

**Specification IDs:** FR-007, FR-008

**Acceptance criteria**
- A repeated `url` returns `409` with `{ "error": { "code": "CONFLICT", ... } }`. (FR-007, FR-008)
- The first bookmark is unchanged. (FR-007)

**Test:** `rejects a duplicate URL` in `tests/bookmarks.test.js`

**Expected files:** `src/routes/bookmarks.js`, `src/models/bookmark.js`

**Out of scope:** other endpoints, persistence, new dependencies

Each criterion cites a specification ID and a test. The issue adds no behavior that the spec lacks.

docs.title: Your issue
docs.text: Write one issue for the whole slice in starter/capstone-handoff.md, in the same shape: goal, specification IDs (FR-001 to FR-008), acceptance criteria with the test for each, expected files, out of scope, and reviewer.

docs.title: Run the baseline
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02
cp -R lab/starter/capstone-project ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02/capstone-project
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02/capstone-project
npm install
npm test -- --runTestsByPath tests/health.test.js
npm test

The failing bookmark tests are your baseline. They are the specification as executable checks, and they fail because the route doesn't exist. Health passes. Write down both results. You're done when the bookmark tests pass. Don't edit them.

docs.title: Phase 3: Prompt Copilot to implement it (40 min)
docs.text:
Paste your issue into Copilot Chat or agent mode with a prompt like this:

Implement this issue in the capstone project. Use only the existing dependencies.
Don't edit anything under tests/.

[paste the issue]

First list the files you will change and the specification ID each change serves.
Then make the change and run npm test. Report the changed files and the test
output.

Read the file list before you let Copilot edit. If it names a file the issue doesn't expect, ask why. Then check that it implements only:

  • route registration;
  • in-memory creation and duplicate lookup;
  • validation of the accepted fields;
  • the documented success and error responses.

If Copilot adds another endpoint, a dependency, or live data, remove it and tighten the prompt.

docs.title: Phase 4: Review, test, and hand off (40 min)
docs.text:
Passing tests are the start of the review. Do these checks in order:

  1. Run the suite. npm test passes, health included.
  2. Check the diff. git diff shows no edits under tests/ and no new entry in package.json.
  3. Trace each specification ID to a test. For each of FR-001 to FR-008, name the test that fails if the rule breaks. A requirement with no test is a gap.
  4. Break it on purpose. Remove the duplicate check, or change the title limit from 200 to 201. The matching test must fail. Restore the change.
  5. Read the responses. Status codes, envelope shape, id, createdAt, updatedAt: null, and the description: null and tags: [] defaults all match the spec. The tests also fix the exact message text, such as url is required. The spec doesn't define it. Note that as a spec gap.
  6. Record deviations from the issue.

Your reviewer then records approve or request changes in starter/capstone-handoff.md. Complete the remaining sections of the handoff.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text: Time Expected state 15 min Specification reviewed 40 min Issue written and baseline recorded 80 min Copilot's patch is in place 105 min Checks 1 to 6 are done 120 min Handoff is complete

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
One capstone-handoff.md with:

  1. the issue, mapped to specification IDs;
  2. a patch summary;
  3. test results, including the baseline and the break-it check;
  4. the reviewer's decision;
  5. deviations and deferred scope;
  6. the next action.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M6-02 trainer guide: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Guide learners through one reviewed POST /api/bookmarks change with GitHub Copilot: specification to issue, issue to prompt, prompt to patch, patch to review. Keep it to one endpoint.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00 to 0:07 Define the one-slice capstone and the four terms 0:07 to 0:15 Review the specification (keep it short) 0:15 to 0:30 Worked example: spec to issue to prompt 0:30 to 0:38 The failing tests as the baseline 0:38 to 0:50 Walk through the patch and review it beyond the trace 0:50 to 1:00 Hand off

docs.title: Teach the boundary
docs.text:
Learners use Copilot to implement POST /api/bookmarks, run the tests, and have a person review the result. Write the non-goals where everyone can see them:

  • no authentication;
  • no persistent storage;
  • no list, read, update, or delete endpoint;
  • no deployment or CI redesign;
  • no new dependency.

docs.title: Define the terms
docs.text:
Spend two minutes on these. They are in the lab README.

  • Synthetic data: made-up bookmarks. Nothing real.
  • Specification ID: FR-001 to FR-008 in lab/starter/bookmark-create-spec.md.
  • Response envelope: { "data": ... } on success, { "error": { "code", "message" } } on failure.
  • Baseline: the test results before the change.

docs.title: Review the specification
docs.text: Keep this to the lab's 15 minutes. Learners check that requirements describe something observable and that technology choices sit under constraints. Ask them to find one ambiguity. The error message text is a good one: the tests fix it, the spec doesn't.

docs.title: Worked example: spec to issue to prompt
docs.text:
Walk through the example in the lab README. Take FR-007 and FR-008, write the issue live, then show the prompt:

Implement this issue in the capstone project. Use only the existing dependencies.
Don't edit anything under tests/.

[paste the issue]

First list the files you will change and the specification ID each change serves.
Then make the change and run npm test. Report the changed files and the test
output.

Point out three things: each criterion cites a spec ID and a test, the prompt asks for the file list before any edit, and the prompt forbids test edits.

docs.title: Frame the baseline
docs.text: The Bookmark tests fail on purpose. They are the spec as executable checks, and they define done. Health passes. Learners record both results and don't edit the tests. If Copilot edits a test to make it pass, that's a review finding.

docs.title: Review beyond the trace
docs.text:
Mapping each criterion to a spec ID is the first pass. Then teach the checks in Phase 4 of the lab:

  1. Run the suite.
  2. Check the diff for test or package.json changes.
  3. Name a test for each specification ID.
  4. Break a rule on purpose and watch its test fail. This shows the test can catch the bug.
  5. Read the responses against the spec.

Don't approve a change with a serious issue because time ran out.

docs.title: Reference assets
docs.text:
• lab/solution/capstone-project/: the creation endpoint and tests.
  • lab/solution/reference-handoff.md: the issue-to-handoff record.
  • lab/starter/capstone-handoff.md: the learner template.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Should learners add the other Bookmark endpoints? No. Note them as deferred scope.

What if Copilot access fails? Write the issue and the prompt anyway. Review the reference patch with the five checks.

What if the tests can't run? Record the command and the failure. Don't approve without test results.
